svg.title: Restricted DG points, nilpotent lifts and finite projective gluing
svg.desc: On the projective line a framed tensor functor has h odd scalar coefficients; the associative operator u has power h plus one zero, so finite representation values lie in the finite-lisse ind-target. Stable operator-image triangles give the full nilpotent lifting comparison. A derived coefficient pullback glues finite projective frame modules and yields infinitesimal cohesiveness of the restricted point functor. The exact bi-infinite shift example prevents extending this gluing assertion to all modules.
svg.text: Full DG restricted points and nilpotent lifting
Smooth projective connected complex X; connected reductive H; every connective DG base.
1. Odd coefficients give one uniform bound — DRD.1–DRD.4
P¹: α = Σ_j e_j a_j, h = dim h; the a_j have total degree −1.
a_j²=0; every word of length h+1 repeats a scalar coefficient.
All finite representation values lie in I_X, on every DG coefficient algebra.
This also holds on every coherent simplex; I_(P¹) is still a proper part of Q_(P¹).
2. The actual stable-image lift — DRD.5–DRD.11
For a derived square-zero extension J → B → A and a full flat-torsor lift:
J ⊗_A E_V → oblv_B(Ẽ_V) → E_V.
Both outside terms lie in I_X; stability puts the middle term there.
Finite nilpotent filtrations and full Postnikov convergence retain every higher map.
Z_restr(B) = Z_restr(A) ×_(Z_dR(A)) Z_dR(B) for nilpotent H⁰(B) → H⁰(A).
3. Glue finite projective frames — DRD.12–DRD.17
R=B×_C D; H⁰(B) → H⁰(C) is surjective with nilpotent kernel.
Proj(R) = Proj(B) ×_(Proj(C)) Proj(D), with full mapping complexes.
H⁰(R) → H⁰(B)×_(H⁰(C))H⁰(D) has square-zero kernel.
Ordinary complements and lifted idempotents give actual finite projective DG modules.
The finite connection atlas and nilpotent lift comparison give restricted infinitesimal gluing.
4. The associative square must remain — DRD.18–DRD.19
U²=[[ab,−2ac],[2bc,−ab]], U³=3abc I₂, U⁴=0.
ab and abc are nonzero exterior basis elements.
The h=3 bound u⁴=0 is sharp; replacing it by u²=0 would be false.
The matrix coefficients use the original graded-commutative scalar signs.
5. A nonzero pair invisible to the unit — DRD.20–DRD.23
B=D=ℂ, C_alg=ℂ⊕ℂη, |η|=−1; R=ℂ[ε]/ε², |ε|=0.
V has one basis vector in every integer degree; T:V → V[1] is invertible.
Transition φ(e_n)=e_n+ηe_(n+1); the pair (V,V,φ) is nonzero.
Its unit Hom is Fib[(v,w) ↦ (v−w,−Tw)] = 0.
It cannot come from an R-module. All-module essential surjectivity fails.
6. Unbounded coefficients retain infinitely many point groups — DRD.24–DRD.26
P¹, H=G_m, A=C[z], |z|=−2: the framed point complex is A[−1].
π_(2r−1)=Cz^r, π_(2r)=0 for r≥1; there is one component.
A (2r−1)-loop is α=z^r dt₁∧…∧dt_(2r−1); u²=0 on every weight.
No lower bound on the coefficient cohomology is imposed.
Effective derived ind-affine charts and their compact connective cotangent calculation are additional.
Proof locators: §§3.119–3.127. Deformation framework: AGKRRV, arXiv:2010.01906v2.
